interest: This file provides valuable insight into the U.S. State Department's internal recordkeeping and historical-legal analysis of Japanese labor migration. It documents how the Treaty Division under Whittington re-examined the history of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation and Japanese emigration policies in early 1932, a pivotal moment in interwar U.S.-Japan relations. Furthermore, the docket sheet serves as an essential archival index, providing specific cross-reference decimal file numbers (894.56, 711.942, and 150.946) to trace broader diplomatic and immigration policy correspondence.
keywords: Treaty of Commerce and Navigation of 1911
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet for State Department decimal file 894.5611 (typed as 894.5G11), concerning emigration from Japan to the United States. It records a single entry, sub-number 8, dated March 19, 1932, documenting a memorandum prepared by Whittington of the Treaty Division regarding the policy and practice of the Japanese Government in relation to the emigration of Japanese laborers to the United States. The entry references a prior Treaty Division memorandum of February 18, 1932 concerning negotiations leading to the conclusion of the February 21, 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation between the United States and Japan, discusses the broader emigration problem, and provides cross-references to related decimal files (894.56, 711.942, and 150.946).
